newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
JANATA DAL AND LEFTIST PARTIES OPPOSE LALOO FACTION ENTRY

The Left Front and the Janata Dal party were against admitting the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJS) party of Laloo Yadav into the ruling United Front. They also wanted Laloo Yadav to resign as the chief minister of Bihar state. The leftist parties maintained that the ministers belonging to Laloo Yadav's party could not continue in the Gujral ministry as long as Yadav who is indicted in a corruption case remained chief minister.
The Economic Times
BOURSE REGULATOR TO TEAM UP WITH RESERVE BANK

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to rope in bourse regulator Security and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to finalise guidelines that will come into effect once the country moved towards capital account convertibility of the rupee. SEBI is being brought into the picture as foreign institutional investors are regulated by both the RBI and the SEBI. The Reserve Bank feels implementation of the capital account convertibility report is a multilateral task and all agencies connected with the issue should be consulted.
WORLD BANK CONSIDERING 38 BLN RUPEE LOAN PROPOSAL

The World Bank is considering a proposal to provide a loan assistance of 38 billion rupees to India for fourlaning certain segments of the National Highway connecting Delhi and Madras with Calcutta. A World Bank official said the Bank was serious about the upcoming road projects on these two corridors of the golden quadrangle. The official said a decision on the loan amount would be taken only after the World Bank assessed the projects. The National Highway Authority of India has already approached the World Bank for a loan assistance.
MEET ON FAST TRACK POWER PROJECTS

The cabinet secretary has called a meeting next week to evaluate the progress of fast track power projects. Issues regarding fuel supply agreements, fuel risk, tax rates and its inclusion in the rate of return are expected to be sorted out at the meeting. It will be attended by representatives of the ministries of power, finance, coal and railways. A few of the fast track projects are still awaiting counter guarantees and approvals by the government at various levels.
Financial Express
FRENCH FIRM PROPOSES 1,000MW NUCLEAR POWER PLANT

French power company Electric de France (EDF) has submitted a proposal to the Power Ministry to set up a 1,000 mw nuclear power project with the Modi group. According to the proposal the EDF will hold a majority stake of 51 percent in the project costing about 50 billion rupees. The remaining 49 percent will have to be shared by the Modi group and the state government under which the project will come up. According to sources in the Power Ministry the ministry has asked the EDF to provide more details on its plans and the technology it had.
Business Standard
BOURSE INDICES SLIDE AGAIN

Sensitive indices across major bourses slid for the third consecutive day due to operator unwinding coupled with selective foreign institutional investors sales. The Bombay bourse closed at 4,183.42, losing 37.60 points over the previous close. The National bourse dipped to 1,183 points losing 0.35 point. Market sources said with many scrips moving out of their no-delivery period and being settled in the current settlement, operators were squaring off their positions.
UNITED STATES HAULS INDIA TO DISPUTE SETTLEMENT FORUM

The United States, Australia and the New Zealand have sought consultations with India under the dispute settlement procedures of the World Trade Organisation (WTO). The three filed separate complaints against India's phase out schedule to remove quantitative restrictions on imports. Diplomatic sources said the European Union, Switzerland and Canada will also file such complaints against India. This is the first time the members sought the help of the dispute settlement mechanism to settle a balance of payment dispute. If a settlement is not reached within 60 days under the mechanism the dispute will be heard by a WTO panel.
BANKS FREE TO SET FOREX TRADING HOURS

The Foreign Exchange Dealers Association decided to free foreign exchange trading hours for banks. The association will shortly issue a circular stating that trading hours will now be left to individual banks. The present trading hours are from 9:30 in the morning to 2:30 in the afternoon (local time) for corporate trading and 9:30 in the morning to four in the evening for inter-bank trading. The clearing time set by the Reserve Bank is four in the evening. Banks will now have to set their own trading hours, which will be determined by their infrastructural capabilities in terms of personnel and back office functions.
The Observer
GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT GROWTH PUT AT 6.8 PCT

The government said the revised estimate for gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1997/98 (April-March) over the previous year would be 6.8 percent as forecast in January. The figure is higher than the one predicted by the Finance Ministry last month. The rise resulted from a higher than expected agricultural growth that offset lower industrial growth. Senior director of the Confederation of the Indian Industries said a higher agricultural growth of 5.7 percent would lower food bills and boost industrial demand in 1997/98.
